requirements.evidence: Migrations match spec: `slug` unique 'entities_slug_unique', softDeletes (create_entities_table.php:17-19); FKs cascadeOnDelete, role default 'employee', stored generated `owner_seq` `case when role = 'owner' then 1 else null end`, unique indexes 'entity_memberships_entity_user_unique' and 'entity_memberships_one_owner' (create_entity_memberships_table.php:15-28). Entity: HasFactory, SoftDeletes, getRouteKeyName 'slug', memberships/users/owner (Entity.php:18-54). EntityMembership role cast to UserRole, owner/admin/employee scopes, entity/user relations. UserRole::manageable() returns [Admin, Employee]. User::memberships/entities/membershipFor(int). Factories with owner/admin/employee states. Both policies implement every rule from the task, including 'owner membership never deletable' before self-removal (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:34-41). docs/database-schema.md drops owner_membership_id as the task asks.

conventions.evidence: Authorization is done in policies under app/Policies; `#[Fillable]` attribute matches the User sibling (Entity.php:14, EntityMembership.php:13), and owner_seq is deliberately left out of it; migrations have reversible down() and generator-style timestamps/names; PHPDoc on public methods; CHANGELOG updated under [Unreleased] (Added + Changed); docs/database-schema.md updated with the invariant and the policies. No Actions are needed because the task has no domain write use cases.

security.evidence: Policies resolve the actor's membership per entity (`membershipFor($membership->entity_id)`), so an owner of another entity gets nothing (tested in EntityPolicyTest.php:47-53 and EntityMembershipPolicyTest.php:56-67). Strict in_array checks against enum cases. The owner invariant is enforced in the DB, not just in app code. Mass assignment is explicit and excludes owner_seq. Only nit: the strict `$membership->user_id === $user->id` (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:41) relies on the driver returning ints, but that fails closed.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/Models/EntityTest.php covers the factories, slug routing, soft delete, slug uniqueness, relations including owner()->first() null/non-null, scopes, membershipFor, the enum, the composite unique, second-owner rejection on insert and on update, multiple owners across entities, the generated column value, cascades and the DB default. The policy tests cover every role with datasets, non-members, owners of other entities, the undeletable owner, self-removal, employee-vs-employee, and gate auto-discovery.

simplicity.evidence: Minimal models and policies. The owner relation is a single hasOne with where (Entity.php:52); the policies share a small private isOwnerOrAdmin helper. The only duplication is that helper appearing in both policies (EntityPolicy.php:52, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:43), which is negligible.

readability.evidence: Clear names and short methods; the migration comment explains why NULLs make the unique index work (create_entity_memberships_table.php:20-21); no dead code or debug output; tests are readable and use datasets.

scope.evidence: Only models, enum, factories, migrations, policies, tests, CHANGELOG and docs/database-schema.md. No routes, session, middleware, pages or translations, as the out-of-scope list requires.

issues.explanation: `$membership->user_id === $user->id` uses strict comparison on an uncast attribute, so a driver that returns numeric strings would wrongly deny self-removal (this fails closed); a `user_id` integer cast or `(int)` would make it robust.
The global helper `memberOf()` is declared in a Pest file and could collide with a same-named helper in another test file; a closure or Pest.php helper would be safer.
The isOwnerOrAdmin logic is duplicated in both policies; acceptable at this size, but it could live on EntityMembership/User later.

review.summary: Adds the entities and entity_memberships tables (with a DB-enforced single owner through a stored generated owner_seq column and a unique index), the Entity/EntityMembership models, the UserRole enum, User relations, factories and both policies, all matching the contract, with thorough Pest tests and updated docs and changelog. Only nits were found, and the change stays within the task's scope, so it can be approved as is.
